headline: Oil Surges on Middle East Attacks While Precious Metals Slide Sharply
paragraphs: Silver suffered the steepest drop today, falling 5.05% to $54.52 per ounce (EUR 48.57) as surging crude prices heightened inflation risks. Brent crude climbed 3.80% to $112.95 per barrel (EUR 100.62) and WTI rose 2.18% to $99.27 after Houthi attacks and strikes on Saudi Arabia raised Middle East tensions and threatened global supplies.

Platinum fell 3.67% to $1565.90 per ounce and palladium dropped 3.43% to $1047.50 following HSBC reducing its 2026 price forecasts for both metals. Gold slid 2.84% to $4032.20 per ounce (EUR 3591.88) as elevated oil costs pressured key technical support while markets weighed interest rate outlooks.

Copper declined 2.24% to $6.40 per pound, pressured by continuing inventory accumulation at the London Metal Exchange. Natural gas dipped 0.86% to $2.77 per MMBtu, capping an 11.23% drop across the week, though the specific cause of this sharp weekly decline is unclear from current news reports.
